root_causes.root_cause: Docling's Heron RT-DETRv2 layout model does not classify bar charts/infographics as PictureItem when the chart is rendered as vector graphics or text-layer numeric fragments rather than raster images. Without PictureItem classification, no <!-- image --> markers are emitted, so the entire downstream picture enrichment pipeline (_recover_picture_results, splice_picture_text_for_tree, _enrich_image_blocks) never runs. This is an upstream Docling model limitation, not a code change in this codebase.
root_causes.code_path: converters.py:pdf_to_markdown_docling -> result.document.export_to_markdown() -> _collect_picture_regions (returns empty for charts Docling didn't classify as PictureItem)
root_causes.suggested_fix: Add a post-Docling heuristic that detects pages with very low text content relative to page area (chart-dense pages) and synthesizes PictureItem regions for them, or implement a secondary chart-detection pass using the existing fitz/pypdfium2 page rendering to identify chart regions that Docling missed. Alternatively, for known chart-heavy documents, force the image-standalone pipeline with OCR on the full page.

root_causes.root_cause: Docling's TableFormer ACCURATE mode drops merged-cell/rowspan content during table reconstruction. The markdown export renders empty cells where merged cells span multiple rows, producing 45-75% empty-cell ratios in benefit overview tables. This is an upstream TableFormer limitation documented in RFC-010 Gap 6a (multi-row header flattening, rowspan info lost before our pipeline). The _flat_parse_table and _forward_fill_leading_column functions in helpers.py only forward-fill column 0, leaving data columns with empty cells intact.
root_causes.code_path: converters.py:pdf_to_markdown_docling -> Docling TableFormer -> export_to_markdown() -> helpers.py:_flat_parse_table -> _forward_fill_leading_column (column 0 only)
root_causes.suggested_fix: Extend _forward_fill_leading_column to optionally forward-fill ALL columns (not just column 0) when a table has high empty-cell ratios (>30%), or implement a post-TableFormer heuristic that detects rowspan patterns (consecutive empty cells in a column below a non-empty cell) and fills them. Alternatively, read the raw PDF text layer for table regions via fitz clip and reconcile with Docling's table structure.

root_causes.root_cause: The world-stats-pocketbook (292 pages) now completes processing thanks to RFC-028 D0 timeout wiring, but Docling's export_to_markdown() produces ~9.4M chars (~31k chars/page vs ~3k expected), a 10x inflation. This is likely Docling duplicating table content in its markdown export (the pocketbook is dense statistical tables on every page). Additionally, 19/20 image markers remain unenriched, likely because the chunked-Docling path's concatenated pic_results misalign with the concatenated markdown's <!-- image --> markers (the splice_picture_text_for_tree guard rejects on count mismatch).
root_causes.code_path: converters.py:_pdf_to_markdown_docling_chunked -> pdf_to_markdown_docling (per chunk) -> Docling export_to_markdown() table duplication; converters.py:splice_picture_text_for_tree marker/region count mismatch guard
root_causes.suggested_fix: (1) Investigate Docling's export_to_markdown() table duplication on dense statistical pages -- if Docling emits both inline table text AND a separate markdown table block for the same content, deduplicate by detecting repeated content blocks within a page boundary. (2) For the 19/20 unenriched images: debug the marker/pic count mismatch in the chunked path -- the chunk-level pic_results may include regions from chunks that timed out and fell back to PyPDF2 (which strips markers), breaking the global alignment. Fix by recounting markers after concatenation and trimming excess pic_results.
